q.t: Find the adverb: The tortoise walked slowly.
q.e: ‘slowly’ tells how the tortoise walked.

q.t: Find the adverb: We will leave tomorrow.
q.e: ‘tomorrow’ tells when — an adverb of time.

q.t: Find the adverb: Please sit here.
q.e: ‘here’ tells where — an adverb of place.

q.t: Find the adverb: She always smiles.
q.e: ‘always’ tells how often — an adverb of frequency.

q.t: Form the adverb from quick.
q.e: Add -ly to the adjective: quick → quickly.

q.t: Fill in: She sings ___.
q.e: It tells how she sings (a verb) → adverb.

q.t: Fill in: He is a ___ driver.
q.e: It describes ‘driver’ (a noun) → adjective.

q.t: What kind of adverb is very in very tall?
q.e: ‘very’ tells how much — degree.

q.t: Fill in: She speaks English ___.
q.e: ‘well’ is the adverb of ‘good’ — it tells how she speaks.

q.t: Find the adverb: The children went outside.
q.e: ‘outside’ tells where they went.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
q.e: Frequency adverbs go after am/is/are/was/were.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
o: He often goes to the library.
He goes often to the library always.
He goes to often the library.
Often he go to the library.
q.e: Frequency adverbs go before the main verb.

q.t: Which word is an adjective, not an adverb?
q.e: ‘friendly’ describes a noun (a friendly dog) even though it ends in -ly.

q.t: Fill in: He works very ___ to pass the exam. (with a lot of effort)
q.e: ‘hard’ = with effort. ‘hardly’ means ‘almost not’.

q.t: What does I could hardly hear him. mean?
o: I could almost not hear him.
I tried hard to hear him.
q.e: ‘hardly’ = almost not at all.

q.t: Comparative of fast (adverb):
q.e: Short adverb → add -er.

q.t: Comparative of carefully:
q.e: -ly adverbs use ‘more’.

q.t: Find the adverb that modifies an adjective: The film was extremely boring.
q.e: ‘extremely’ tells how boring — it adds to the adjective.

q.t: Fill in: The box is ___ heavy for me to lift.
q.e: ‘too … to’ means more than is possible: I cannot lift it.

q.t: Fill in: He is old ___ to vote.
q.e: ‘enough’ comes after the adjective: old enough.

q.t: Choose the correct order: She sang ___.
o: beautifully at the concert last night
last night beautifully at the concert
at the concert last night beautifully
last night at the concert beautifully
q.e: At the end of a sentence: manner → place → time (how, where, when).

q.t: Fill in: I haven't seen her ___. (recently)
q.e: ‘lately’ = recently. ‘late’ = not on time.

q.t: Fill in: I have ___ been to Japan.
q.e: With a helping verb, the frequency adverb goes after the first helper: have never been.

q.t: Superlative of badly:
q.e: badly – worse – worst (irregular).

q.t: Find the error: She dances very good.
q.e: It describes how she dances (verb) → adverb ‘well’.

q.t: Is fast an adjective or adverb in He ran fast.?
q.e: It tells how he ran → adverb. (In ‘a fast car’ it is an adjective.)

q.t: Fill in: The tea is ___ hot to drink.
q.e: ‘too … to’ shows that something cannot happen. ‘very hot to drink’ is wrong.

q.t: Find the adverb that modifies another adverb: She spoke rather softly.
q.e: ‘rather’ tells how softly — it modifies the adverb ‘softly’.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
o: He is clever enough to solve it.
He is enough clever to solve it.
He is clever too to solve it.
He enough is clever to solve it.
q.e: ‘enough’ goes after the adjective.

q.t: Fill in: He is a ___ runner; he runs ___.
q.e: ‘fast’ is both the adjective and the adverb; ‘fastly’ is not a word.

q.t: Find the adverb: The lovely girl answered the question confidently.
q.e: ‘lovely’ describes the girl (adjective); ‘confidently’ describes how she answered.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
o: I am feeling good today well.
q.e: ‘well’ here means healthy — used after a linking verb as an adjective.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
q.e: ‘smell’ is a linking verb here (the flowers have a sweet smell), so an adjective follows.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
q.e: ‘hardly’ is already negative; adding ‘never’ or ‘not’ makes a double negative.

q.t: Fill in: Of all the runners, Mohan ran the ___.
q.e: Out of all → superlative of the adverb ‘fast’: fastest.

q.t: Find the error: She is enough intelligent to win.
q.e: ‘enough’ comes after an adjective.

q.t: What kind of adverb is upstairs in He went upstairs.?
q.e: It tells where he went.

q.t: Choose the sentence where only means ‘nobody else but Ravi’.
q.e: Put ‘only’ right before the word it limits. ‘Only Ravi’ = no one else.

q.t: Fill in: Seldom ___ such a beautiful sight.
q.e: When a negative adverb (seldom, never, hardly) starts a sentence, the helping verb comes before the subject, as in a question.

q.t: Fill in: She did ___ in the test than I expected.
q.e: Comparative of the adverb ‘well’ is ‘better’.
